verdict.rationale: Ubuntu's own documentation lists a built-in screen reader ('Get started with the screen reader', 'Read the screen aloud', 'Read the screen in Braille') and other accessibility tools: contrast, text size, magnification, keyboard navigation, and bounce/slow/sticky keys. The evidence is only documentation headings, though, and nothing shows these tools work during installation or first-run setup, which is what 'get started with the OS' implies. missing for 10: evidence that the screen reader and accessibility tools are available in the installer/first-boot setup, detail beyond doc titles on how the tools are enabled and used, independent or hands-on corroboration of screen-reader quality.

support.subject: As a switcher, I can use built-in screen readers and accessibility tools to get started with the OS

citations.quote: Get started with the screen reader
Screen reader ... Read the screen aloud ... Read the screen in Braille
Adjust the contrast ... Change text size on the screen ... Magnify a screen area
Navigate the interface using the keyboard ... Turn on bounce keys ... Turn on slow keys ... Turn on sticky keys
